item.title: Open call: 2026 METRO FM Music Awards
item.description: The METRO FM Music Awards (MMAs) in South Africa have opened entries for their 2026 edition, inviting eligible South African artists and record companies to submit music released during the current eligibility period. The awards recognise achievements in the South African recording industry over the past year and form part of METRO FM’s annual music honours. Entries are underway and close on 3 February 2026. item.title: Tanzania: Alikiba appoints Kenyan executive Benjamin Otwal as new manager
item.description: Tanzanian musician Ali Kiba has appointed Kenyan music executive Benjamin Otwal as his new manager, a move that signals a shift in his management strategy as he seeks to expand his reach within East Africa and in international markets. The appointment follows a period of professional collaboration between the two, particularly during Ali Kiba’s recent engagements in Kenya. item.title: Kilele Summit 2026 set for Nairobi with international, regional music line-up
item.description: The third edition of the Kilele Summit is scheduled to take place in Nairobi from 23 to 28 February 2026, bringing together musicians, technologists, and culture workers from across East Africa and beyond. Known for its blend of music, art, and culture, the summit features a combination of performances, workshops, installations, and panel discussions. item.title: Napster shuts down music streaming service to focus on AI assistants
item.description: Napster, the once-pioneering music streaming platform, has abruptly ended its music streaming operations following its acquisition by AI company Infinite Reality, signalling a significant shift in the company’s business model towards artificial intelligence. Users reported that the service cut off while they were actively streaming music, replacing the player with a splash screen stating: “Napster is no longer a music streaming service. item.title: Spotify to end access to ‘Basic’ music-only plan for subscribers who cancel
item.description: Spotify has introduced a significant restriction to its music-only ‘Basic’ subscription, confirming that subscribers who cancel the plan will permanently lose access to it, raising questions about whether the company is effectively phasing out the tier and further reducing songwriter royalties. The change follows Spotify’s decision in late 2023 to integrate audiobooks into its Premium Individual, Family and Duo plans. item.title: Soundstripe, PopArabia launch MENA songwriting camps in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Soundstripe has partnered with Abu Dhabi-based independent music company PopArabia to run a series of songwriting camps aimed at artists and songwriters from the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), marking the US music licensing platform’s first such initiative outside the United States. The first camp was held in Abu Dhabi in October and brought together artists from the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Algeria, Morocco, Iraq, Lebanon and Sudan. item.title: UMG appoints James Steven as chief communications officer
item.description: Universal Music Group (UMG) has appointed James Steven as executive vice President and chief communications officer, effective 26 January. In the role, Steven will lead the company’s internal and external communications and oversee communications functions across UMG’s operating companies worldwide. item.title: Ghana: MOLIY shares new single Backie
item.description: Ghanaian-American artist MOLIY has released her latest single, ‘Backie’, accompanied by a live VEVO performance. item.title: Universal Music Group partners NVIDIA to advance responsible AI in music
item.description: Universal Music Group (UMG) has announced a collaboration with technology company NVIDIA to develop AI-driven tools for music discovery, creation, and fan engagement. The partnership will leverage NVIDIA’s AI infrastructure alongside UMG’s extensive music catalogue, which spans millions of tracks across genres and eras. item.title: The controversial rise of AI in tech-driven Afro-house
item.description: AI is challenging the authenticity of Afro-house while raising serious copyright questions, fuelling debate around ownership and artistic integrity.
